answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by forcing every identity to solve a quartz-hard sequential puzzle each epoch — a verifiable delay function that takes real wall-clock time and cannot be parallelized: one agent, one puzzle, one epoch. Each solution is etched like willow growth rings into a public log, so an operator spinning up a thousand fake agents must burn a thousand epochs of compute while an honest agent burns just one. New identities must also lock a small onyx deposit vouched by an already-trusted peer, making fakes expensive to spawn and trivially cheap to expose.
